extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of satirical/renaissance humorous prose (general educated readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles embedded in a satirical Renaissance prose (Rabelaisian) on what counts as good questions, answers, conduct, and literary style — useful for producing or judging ribald, convivial, and plain-spoken comic prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem clarity (Peripatetics' rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Peripatetics have wisely made a rule that all problems, questions, and doubts which are offered to be solved ought to be certain, clear, and intelligible.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions posed for solution should be precise and understandable (Pantagruel challenges 'What do you mean by dog-sleep?'). Avoid vague or ill-defined problems if you expect useful answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and practical answers over pedantic cant
rubrics_metrics.description: “My answer shall be short, not to tire you with a long needless train of pedantic cant.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer short, direct, practical responses to long-winded learned exposition. The text exemplifies answering by action (signs/gestures) rather than by verbose rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer to match audience needs: 'the belly has no ears'
rubrics_metrics.description: “The belly has no ears, nor is it to be filled with fair words; you shall be answered to content by signs and gestures.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor communication to what the audience actually needs — when practical relief (food, action) is sought, rhetorical flourish is irrelevant. Example: instead of fine words to hungry men, give them food or a demonstrative sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose elevated/serious art over trivial or vulgar entertainments
rubrics_metrics.description: “the wise and studious ought not to give their minds to trivial or vulgar music, but to that which is celestial, divine, angelical, more abstracted…" (allegory of elder wood remote from cock-crowing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic judgement: cultivate refined, lofty, or 'celestial' tastes rather than vulgar or trivial diversions — the allegory of elder-wood distant from cocks stresses selection of higher forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer plain, merry, accessible writing to florid, obscure learnedness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prologue critiques "Whole cartloads of books... florid, flourishing, and flowery ... tiresome, dull, soporiferous..." and praises “these merry and fructifying Pantagruelian books” and a “plain ditty... rather than be thought deaf among so many pretty poets.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary criterion: avoid overly florid, obscure, or pedantic prose; favor lively, fruitful, plain, and amusing writing that engages readers rather than impresses with learned opacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heed inner promptings / intuitive caution (Socratic daemon)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Whenever I have felt such a motion within me I have found myself happy in avoiding what it directed me to shun… As much, said Epistemon, is related of the daemon of Socrates.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical decision rule: trust well-tested internal promptings or intuition (illustrated by Pantagruel avoiding an island) as a legitimate guide to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviviality, food and drink as remedies and performance enhancers
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages asserting that good bread, cool delicious wine, and dainties remove pains and perturbations and that a man is heavier when fasting than when he has eaten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral/effectiveness guideline (humorously asserted): feeding and convivial drinking relieve melancholy, improve morale, and enable better performance (e.g., shorten a calm at sea by carousing). Use conviviality as a practical, social remedy in narrative or social situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical hours / regimen advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians say the canonical hours are: "To rise at five, to dine at nine, To sup at five, to sleep at nine."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive lifestyle rule presented as salutary routine; in context serves as an exemplum of sober regimen and the 'right' timing for bodily needs — can be used as a normative detail in character portrayal or conduct recommendations.
